Background (from the session that started this one):
Guardian is a hackathon project (neatHack, team huma1nity, deadline 12 Oct 2026 11:55 PM IST): a FastAPI service that checks every AI agent tool call with Jev (TypeSafe AI System One) and returns ALLOW, BLOCK or ESCALATE. It traces to NeatLogs, reads sessions with the Entire CLI, and explains blocks with DeepSeek on Modal. The repo is public at github.com/MD-Sharik/guardian; the latest pushed commit is e2336cf, and 84 tests pass. The existing docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is a single mixed document. The user asked for a high-level and a low-level architecture. This session's transcript will be attached as the project's Entire checkpoint (a required hackathon artifact), which is why it must stay free of credentials, screenshots and personal data. The coordinating session will attach the checkpoint and push after this session commits.

Task:
Write Guardian's architecture as two documents, a high-level design and a low-level design, grounded in the code in this repository (C:\Users\sharik\guardian), then commit them. Do not push.

Files:
- Rewrite docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as the high-level design (keep this path: README.md and other docs link to it). At its top, link to the low-level design.
- Create docs/ARCHITECTURE-LOW-LEVEL.md as the low-level design.
- In README.md, only adjust the existing "## Architecture" section so it points to both documents. Keep any diagram there, and don't touch other sections.

High-level design (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), for a judge or new engineer reading in five minutes:
- What Guardian is and the problem it solves (a pre-execution checkpoint between an AI agent and its tools).
- System context: agent (Antigravity via hooks, LangGraph via protect()), Guardian service, Jev (TypeSafe AI System One), NeatLogs, Entire CLI, the LLM explainer (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Modal, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), the dashboard, and the human reviewer.
- Components and responsibilities: guardian-service, guardian-sdk (client, protect, Antigravity hook), dashboard, demo-agent.
- Main flows: ALLOW, BLOCK, ESCALATE with human approve/reject/expiry/handoff, the read-only fast path, and Jev unreachable (escalate, never guess).
- What happens synchronously (Jev + policy) versus in the background (Entire, explainer, NeatLogs trace).
- Deployment view: the local setup (service on 127.0.0.1:8000, dashboard on :3000, SQLite file, CLIs, external APIs).
- Failure behaviour and trust boundaries.
- How each sponsor tool is used.
- Mermaid diagrams: a system-context or component diagram, plus a sequence diagram of one decision.

Low-level design (docs/ARCHITECTURE-LOW-LEVEL.md), precise enough to reimplement:
- Module map with file paths and one-line responsibilities.
- Data model: EvaluateRequest, ActionContext, Decision (every field), JevSignals, JevResult, TraceRef, Explanation, statuses, and the decision state machine as a Mermaid stateDiagram.
- API contract: every endpoint in guardian-service/app/main.py with request and response shapes and error codes, plus the SSE event format.
- The Jev request: how state and typed questions are built (Noul / Choice / Score, output_ok only for writes), how answers become signals, and the confidence formula.
- Policy: every rule in policy.py with its threshold, environment variable and default, rule precedence, and the fast-path regex (GUARDIAN_FAST_PATH_TOOLS, full match).
- Background enrichment order, and the NeatLogs payload shapes: the decision span tree, the agent run trace (demo-agent/run_trace.py), and the replay trace (guardian-service/app/replay.py), plus the retry rules (5xx and network errors retried, 4xx not) and POST /traces/retry.
- SDK internals: check/acheck, long-poll waiting, fail_open, the refusal message prefix, and reporting results.
- The Antigravity hook protocol: stdin fields, the stdout decision mapping, and fail-closed behaviour.
- Storage: the SQLite schema. A configuration reference table of every environment variable read by config.py, the SDK, the hook and the demo agent.
- Concurrency notes, and how the tests are organised.

Rules:
- Every statement must match the code. Read the source rather than guessing. Where the code is ambiguous, say so instead of inventing behaviour.
- Plain, direct English: short sentences, no marketing language. Tables for reference material.
- Mermaid must render on GitHub: quote labels that contain punctuation, and avoid HTML in labels.
- Do not open, print or quote .env, and don't look for credentials anywhere. Do not make live calls to Jev, Modal or NeatLogs, and don't start or stop the running Guardian service or dashboard; this is documentation work only. Don't take screenshots or add images.
- When done, commit only the files you changed, with a clear message whose last line is:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Do not push and do not amend existing commits.
- Finish by reporting the commit SHA and a short summary of what each document covers.

# Guardian architecture Guardian is a checkpoint between an AI agent and its tools. Every tool call is sent to Guardian before it runs; Guardian asks Jev typed questions about it, turns the answers into a verdict, and returns ALLOW, BLOCK or ESCALATE. Everything else (explanations, traces) happens after the verdict, so the agent only ever waits for Jev and the policy. ## Components ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph agents["Agents"] agy["Antigravity (agy)"] -- "PreToolUse / PostToolUse
.agents/hooks.json" --> hook["guardian-antigravity-hook"] lg["LangGraph / LangChain agent"] -- "protect(tools)" --> sdk["guardian-sdk"] any["Any language"] -- "HTTP" --> api hook --> sdk end sdk -- "POST /evaluate" --> api subgraph service["guardian-service · FastAPI"] api["REST + SSE"] --> jevc["jev_client.py"] jevc --> policy["policy.py"] policy --> db[("SQLite")] policy -. "BLOCK / ESCALATE" .-> entc["entire_client.py"] entc --> expl["explainer.py"] policy --> nlt["neatlogs_tracer.py"] end jevc <--> jev[("Jev · TypeSafe AI
System One API")] entc <--> entire[("Entire CLI
sessions + checkpoints")] expl <--> llm[("DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
on Modal")] nlt --> neatlogs[("NeatLogs
HTTP ingest")] api -- "SSE /stream" --> ui["dashboard · Next.js"] ui -- "approve / reject" --> api ``` | Part | Path | Responsibility | |---|---|---| | Service | [`guardian-service/app/`](../guardian-service/app) | FastAPI app: `/evaluate`, approvals, history, SSE stream, health, `doctor` | | Jev adapter | [`adapters/jev_client.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/jev_client.py) | Builds the state and typed questions, calls `system_one` through the official `typesafe-sdk`, flattens the answers | | Policy | [`policy.py`](../guardian-service/app/policy.py) | Thresholds → ALLOW / BLOCK / ESCALATE, with every reason recorded | | Entire adapter | [`adapters/entire_client.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/entire_client.py) | Reads the agent's session and latest checkpoint with the `entire` CLI's JSON output | | Explainer | [`adapters/explainer.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/explainer.py) | One OpenAI-compatible chat completion that turns decision + session into three plain-English lines | | Tracer | [`adapters/neatlogs_tracer.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/neatlogs_tracer.py) | One nested trace per decision via NeatLogs HTTP ingest | | Storage | [`db.py`](../guardian-service/app/db.py) | SQLite, one JSON row per decision | | SDK | [`guardian-sdk/guardian/`](../guardian-sdk/guardian) | `protect()` for LangChain tools, `GuardianClient`, and the Antigravity hook | | Dashboard | [`dashboard/`](../dashboard) | Next.js 16 + Tailwind 4: setup, home, decisions, approvals, sessions, policy, integrations | | Example agent | [`demo-agent/`](../demo-agent) | LangGraph agent driven by the LLM endpoint, sandboxed tools | ## One decision, step by step ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as Agent participant S as SDK / hook participant G as guardian-service participant J as Jev participant D as Dashboard participant B as Background A->>S: tool call (name, args) S->>G: POST /evaluate (tool, args, task, reasoning, session) G->>G: fill recent steps from this session G->>J: state + questions: safe (Noul), on_task (Noul), risk (Choice), severity (Score), output_ok (Noul, writes only) J-->>G: typed answers with probabilities and confidence G->>G: policy → verdict + reasons, saved to SQLite G-->>D: SSE "decision" G-->>S: verdict alt ALLOW S->>A: run the tool, then report the result else BLOCK S->>A: refusal message with Guardian's reasons else ESCALATE S->>G: long-poll /decisions/{id}/wait D->>G: POST /approve/{id} or /reject/{id} G-->>S: approved / rejected end G->>B: for BLOCK / ESCALATE B->>B: Entire session → LLM explanation → NeatLogs trace B-->>D: SSE "decision" (updated) ``` ## What Jev is asked The state is JSON: the agent, its task, its stated reasoning, the proposed action (tool, description, arguments truncated to 2,000 characters) and its last five steps. Questions are evaluated in parallel against that state: | Name | Type | Question | |---|---|---| | `safe` | Noul | The action can't destroy or corrupt data, leak secrets, damage the environment, or do something irreversible the task didn't ask for | | `on_task` | Noul | The action is a sensible step toward the agent's task | | `risk` | Choice | none · data loss · exfiltration · system damage · unclear | | `severity` | Score | negligible · minor · serious · critical, if it's a mistake | | `output_ok` | Noul | Only for writes: the content is complete and correct | **Confidence** is the least certain answer: the Choice and Score confidences Jev returns, and |2·P(safe) − 1| for the Noul, as TypeSafe's docs suggest. ## The policy | Verdict | When (defaults, all configurable in `.env`) | |---|---| | BLOCK | P(safe) < 0.30, or impact ≥ 2.3 / 3, or a dangerous risk category with p ≥ 0.70 | | ESCALATE | confidence < 0.50, 0.30 ≤ P(safe) < 0.75, impact ≥ 1.5, P(on task) < 0.40 with impact ≥ 1, written content P(ok) < 0.40, risk "unclear", or Jev unreachable | | ALLOW | none of the above; an off-task action with negligible impact is allowed with a note | Every rule that fires becomes a reason; the strictest verdict wins. If Jev can't be reached, the action goes to a human. Guardian never guesses. **Fast path.** Tools matching `GUARDIAN_FAST_PATH_TOOLS` (read-only tool names) are allowed without a Jev call. The decision is still stored, streamed and traced, with `checked: false`. **Replay.** Each decision stores Jev's typed answers, so `python dev.py replay` can re-score history under the current thresholds and fast path, and show which verdicts would change and how many Jev calls and escalations that saves, without calling Jev. The off-task rule above came from doing exactly that with a live run in which three harmless reads were escalated; see [hackathon.md](../hackathon.md). **Traces.** If NeatLogs ingest fails, Guardian retries 5xx and network errors, keeps the payload on the decision, and `POST /traces/retry` re-sends it later. A 4xx is the payload's fault and isn't retried. ## Antigravity integration Antigravity runs `guardian-antigravity-hook pre` before every tool call and `post` after it ([hooks contract](https://antigravity.google/docs/hooks/)). The hook: - maps `toolCall.name` / `toolCall.args` to the action, the `conversationId` to the session (also the Entire session ID), and the workspace path to Entire's repository; - reads the user's latest prompt and the agent's latest message from the transcript, best effort; - answers `allow`, `deny` (with Guardian's reasons, which the model sees), or, on ESCALATE, waits for the dashboard and falls back to Antigravity's own `force_ask` prompt if nobody answers; - always prints one JSON decision and exits 0, because Antigravity denies the call when a hook fails. ## Traces Each decision becomes one NeatLogs trace: ``` guardian.evaluate WORKFLOW ├─ jev.system_one GUARDRAIL neatlogs.guardrail.passed / score ├─ guardian.policy CHAIN signals → verdict + reasons ├─ entire.session_context RETRIEVER (BLOCK / ESCALATE) └─ guardian.explainer LLM (BLOCK / ESCALATE) ``` Guardian uses NeatLogs' HTTP ingest (`POST /v1/trace`) because the `neatlogs` Python SDK requires Python < 3.14. Empty fields are omitted, because the ingest rejects `null`. ## Failure behaviour | What fails | What happens | |---|---| | Jev | The action is escalated to a human, with the error shown | | Explainer | The decision stands; the drawer shows the error instead of an explanation | | Entire | The explanation is written without session context; the reason is shown | | NeatLogs | The trace is kept on the decision and marked failed | | Guardian itself (Antigravity) | The hook answers `force_ask`, so the human decides in the terminal | | Guardian itself (SDK) | Calls are refused unless `fail_open=True` | ====== # Guardian **A real-time reliability and safety layer for AI agents.** Guardian sits between an agent and its tools. Before any tool call runs, it asks **Jev**, TypeSafe AI's "System One" decision model, a set of typed questions: *Is this action safe? What kind of risk is it? How bad is the impact if it's a mistake? Is the content being written good enough?* Jev answers with calibrated probabilities and confidence scores, and Guardian's policy turns them into one of three signals: **ALLOW** (run it), **BLOCK** (refuse it and tell the agent why), or **ESCALATE** (pause the agent until a human approves or rejects it in the dashboard). Every decision is traced to **NeatLogs**. When something is blocked or escalated, Guardian pulls the agent's captured session from **Entire** and has an LLM (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Modal) explain in plain English why the agent made that move. It plugs into **Google Antigravity** through Antigravity's own hook system, and into any LangGraph/LangChain agent in two lines: ```python from guardian import protect tools = protect(tools, agent_name="my-agent") ``` [![Guardian launch video: an agent types rm -rf ./* and Guardian blocks it before it runs](brag-output/brag.jpg)](brag-output/brag.mp4) *22-second launch video: [brag-output/brag.mp4](brag-output/brag.mp4)* ## Verified live On 11 October 2026, one agent action (`run_command rm -rf ./*`) went through the whole pipeline against the real services: | Step | Result | |---|---| | Jev (`jev-1.13.0`) | **BLOCK**: P(safe) 0.11, data-loss risk 0.96, impact 2.5 / 3 critical; answered in 603 ms | | Explainer (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Modal) | *"It wipes all files, not just the cache, risking critical data loss. Safer: clear only the specific cache directory."* | | Entire CLI 0.11.4 | Ran against the project; reported that no session had been captured there yet | | NeatLogs | Trace accepted, with all five spans visible in the NeatLogs dashboard | Jev was reached through jev-ai.pro, a third-party host of TypeSafe's System One API. TypeSafe directly, OpenCode Zen and OpenRouter use the same code with a different `JEV_BASE_URL`. A live Antigravity session hasn't been run yet; the hook is tested end to end against a running Guardian with Antigravity's documented payloads. ### Live agent runs, and what they changed The LangGraph example agent, driven by DeepSeek on Modal, was given *"wipe the whole workspace with `rm -rf ./*`"*. It investigated first and proposed deleting only the stale lock file. But Guardian escalated three harmless reads to a human: Jev rated them safe with negligible impact, yet "off task". So we refined the policy and added a fast path for read-only tools, then replayed the run's real Jev answers through both (`python dev.py replay`): | Same session, same Jev answers | Before (live) | After | |---|---|---| | Jev calls | 9 | **6** | | Escalated to a human | 4 | **1** (the uncertain delete) | | `rm -rf ./*` (all recorded decisions) | blocked | still blocked | A Jev check costs about 940 input tokens and 761 ms (median, measured); a fast-path decision takes 0.9 ms. Each run is sent to NeatLogs as one trace: every LLM call with its tokens, every tool call, and Guardian's verdict under each checked call. Guardian's own decision traces share the run's session ID, so NeatLogs groups them. The run's totals print at the end and are saved to `evidence/runs/`. A tool that fails returns its error to the agent instead of ending the run. If NeatLogs is unreachable, `python demo-agent/run.py --resend` sends saved run traces later. File tools refuse paths outside `demo-agent/workspace`, `run_shell` only runs `ls`, `cat`, `echo` and screened Python scripts and refuses everything else, and `http_request` only sends GET requests. Guardian records the input tokens of every check. The state holds the agent, its task, its stated reasoning, the proposed action and its recent steps. import time

import pytest

import fake_jev


def evaluate(client, tool, session="s1", **args):
    resp = client.post("/evaluate", json={
        "agent_name": "test-agent",
        "tool": tool,
        "args": args,
        "session_id": session,
        "context": {"task": "Fix the greeting", "reasoning": "Testing"},
    })
    assert resp.status_code == 200, resp.text
    return resp.json()


def test_health_reports_what_is_configured(client):
    body = client.get("/health").json()
    assert body["modes"] == {"jev": "live", "neatlogs": "off", "entire": "off", "explainer": "off"}


def test_allow(client):
    d = evaluate(client, "read_file", path="README.md")
    assert d["verdict"] == "ALLOW" and d["status"] == "allowed"
    assert d["jev"]["model"] == "jev-test" and d["jev_error"] is None
    assert d["trace"] is None and d["explanation"] is None  # NeatLogs and the explainer are off
    after = client.post(f"/decisions/{d['id']}/result", json={"ok": True, "output": "hello"}).json()
    assert after["result"]["output"] == "hello"


def test_block(client):
    d = evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="rm -rf ./*")
    assert d["verdict"] == "BLOCK" and d["status"] == "blocked"
    assert d["explanation_pending"] is False  # explainer off: nothing to wait for
    assert any("unsafe" in r for r in d["reasons"])


def test_escalate_approve(client):
    d = evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="python scripts/migrate_db.py --apply")
    assert d["verdict"] == "ESCALATE" and d["status"] == "pending"
    assert client.get(f"/decisions/{d['id']}/wait", params={"timeout": 0.2}).json()["status"] == "pending"

    approved = client.post(f"/approve/{d['id']}", json={"by": "tester"}).json()
    assert approved["status"] == "approved" and approved["resolved_by"] == "tester"
    assert client.get(f"/decisions/{d['id']}/wait").json()["status"] == "approved"
    assert client.post(f"/reject/{d['id']}").json()["status"] == "approved"  # resolving twice is a no-op


def test_escalate_reject_and_handoff(client):
    d = evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="python scripts/migrate_db.py --apply")
    assert client.post(f"/reject/{d['id']}").json()["status"] == "rejected"

    d = evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="python scripts/migrate_db.py --apply")
    handed = client.post(f"/handoff/{d['id']}", json={"by": "antigravity prompt"}).json()
    assert handed["status"] == "handed_off" and handed["resolved_by"] == "antigravity prompt"


def test_jev_outage_escalates_to_a_human(make_client):
    client = make_client(fake_jev.down)
    d = evaluate(client, "read_file", path="README.md")
    assert d["verdict"] == "ESCALATE" and d["status"] == "pending"
    assert d["jev"] is None and d["jev_error"]
    assert "human must decide" in d["reasons"][0]


def test_fast_path_allows_read_only_tools_without_asking_jev(make_client):
    calls = []

    def counting(request):
        calls.append(request)
        return fake_jev.handler(request)

    client = make_client(counting, GUARDIAN_FAST_PATH_TOOLS="read_file|list_dir")
    d = evaluate(client, "read_file", path="README.md")
    assert d["verdict"] == "ALLOW" and d["status"] == "allowed"
    assert d["checked"] is False and d["jev"] is None and d["jev_error"] is None
    assert calls == []
    # Names must match in full, and everything else is still checked.
    assert evaluate(client, "read_file_and_delete", path="x")["checked"] is True
    assert evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="rm -rf ./*")["verdict"] == "BLOCK"
    assert len(calls) == 2


def test_failed_traces_are_resent_once_neatlogs_is_back(make_client, monkeypatch):
    import httpx

    from app import guardian
    from app.adapters.neatlogs_tracer import NeatLogsTracer

    up = {"value": False}

    def neatlogs(request):
        if not up["value"]:
            return httpx.Response(503, text="Service Temporarily Unavailable")
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"trace_id": "tr_late"})

    monkeypatch.setattr(guardian, "NeatLogsTracer",
                        lambda s: NeatLogsTracer(s, transport=httpx.MockTransport(neatlogs), backoff_s=0))
    client = make_client(NEATLOGS_API_KEY="nl-key")
    d = evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="rm -rf ./*")
    for _ in range(100):  # the trace is sent in the background
        trace = client.get(f"/decisions/{d['id']}").json()["trace"]
        if trace:
            break
        time.sleep(0.05)
    assert trace["mode"] == "error" and "503" in trace["error"]

    up["value"] = True
    assert client.post("/traces/retry").json() == {"failed_before": 1, "sent": 1, "still_failing": 0}
    assert client.get(f"/decisions/{d['id']}").json()["trace"]["trace_id"] == "tr_late"

    assert client.post("/traces/retry").status_code == 409


def test_replay_rescores_recorded_decisions_without_jev(make_client):
    from app.config import Settings
    from app.db import DecisionStore
    from app.replay import replay

    client = make_client()
    evaluate(client, "read_file", path="README.md")
    evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="rm -rf ./*")
    evaluate(client, "run_shell", command="python scripts/migrate_db.py --apply")

    assert (t["block_before"], t["block_after"]) == (1, 1)  # the dangerous step is still blocked

    store.close()

    payload = trace_payload(report, "s1", "guardian")
    assert payload["attributes"] == {"neatlogs.session.id": "s1"}

    assert [d["id"] for d in client.get("/decisions").json()][:2] == [second["id"], first["id"]]

    assert client.get("/decisions").json() == []

# Guardian architecture: high-level design

This is the five-minute overview. The precise reference (module map, data model, API contract, the Jev request, every policy rule, trace payloads, SDK and hook internals, storage, configuration and tests) is the **[low-level design](ARCHITECTURE-LOW-LEVEL.md)**.

## What Guardian is

AI agents call tools that change real things: they run shell commands, write files and send HTTP requests. One wrong call, such as `rm -rf ./*` or a request that uploads a secret, can't be undone.

Guardian is a checkpoint that sits between an agent and its tools. Before a tool call runs, the agent sends it to Guardian. Guardian asks **Jev** (TypeSafe AI's System One decision model) a fixed set of typed questions about the call, turns the answers into a verdict with a configurable policy, and returns one of three answers:

- **ALLOW**: run the tool.
- **BLOCK**: don't run it. The agent gets a refusal with Guardian's reasons and has to choose another approach.
- **ESCALATE**: pause the agent until a human approves or rejects the call in the dashboard.

Design rules that shape everything below:

1. The agent waits only for Jev and the policy. Session lookup, explanations and tracing run after the verdict.
2. Guardian never guesses. If Jev can't answer, the call goes to a human.
3. Every decision is stored with Jev's raw answers, so a policy change can be replayed against real history before it ships.
4. Integrations other than Jev are optional. Each shows as `off` until configured; nothing is simulated.

## System context

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    human(["Human reviewer"])

    subgraph agents["Agents"]
        agy["Antigravity agent"]
        lg["LangGraph agent"]
        other["Any HTTP client"]
    end

    subgraph guardian["Guardian"]
        hook["guardian-antigravity-hook"]
        sdk["guardian-sdk: protect() and GuardianClient"]
        svc["guardian-service (FastAPI)"]
        db[("SQLite decision store")]
        ui["Dashboard (Next.js)"]
    end

    jev[("Jev: TypeSafe AI System One")]
    entire["Entire CLI"]
    llm[("LLM explainer: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Modal")]
    nl[("NeatLogs")]

    agy -- "PreToolUse / PostToolUse hooks" --> hook
    hook --> sdk
    lg -- "protect(tools)" --> sdk
    sdk -- "POST /evaluate" --> svc
    other -- "POST /evaluate" --> svc
    svc -- "state + typed questions" --> jev
    svc --> db
    svc -. "BLOCK / ESCALATE: read session" .-> entire
    svc -. "BLOCK / ESCALATE: explain" .-> llm
    svc -. "one trace per decision" .-> nl
    lg -. "one trace per run" .-> nl
    svc -- "SSE /stream" --> ui
    ui -- "approve / reject" --> svc
    human --> ui
```

Solid lines are on the agent's critical path. Dotted lines run in the background.

| External system | What Guardian uses it for |
|---|---|
| **Jev** (TypeSafe AI System One) | The decision model. One `system_one` request per checked tool call, through the official `typesafe-sdk`. Any host that serves the same API works (`JEV_BASE_URL`): TypeSafe directly, OpenCode Zen, OpenRouter, or a third-party host. |
| **NeatLogs** | Observability. One trace per decision, one per example-agent run, and one per replay comparison, sent to the HTTP ingest. |
| **Entire CLI** | The agent's captured session (prompts, transcript, checkpoint), read for BLOCK and ESCALATE decisions so the explanation can say *why* the agent tried the call. |
| **LLM explainer** | Turns a decision and its Entire session into three plain-English lines. Configured for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on a Modal endpoint; any OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint works. The example agent uses the same endpoint as its planner. |
| **Antigravity** | An agent host. Guardian plugs into its documented hook system. |
| **Human reviewer** | Decides ESCALATE calls in the dashboard. |

## Components

| Component | Path | Responsibility | Runs as |
|---|---|---|---|
| guardian-service | [`guardian-service/app/`](../guardian-service/app) | Evaluates calls (Jev + policy), stores and streams decisions, resolves escalations, enriches decisions in the background. Also ships two CLIs: `doctor` (checks each integration with a real call) and `replay` (re-scores history offline). | One uvicorn process with one asyncio event loop |
| guardian-sdk | [`guardian-sdk/guardian/`](../guardian-sdk/guardian) | `GuardianClient` (calls `/evaluate`, long-polls escalations, reports results), `protect()` (wraps LangChain / LangGraph tools), and the `guardian-antigravity-hook` command | A library inside the agent's process. The hook is one short-lived process per tool call. |
| dashboard | [`dashboard/`](../dashboard) | Next.js 16, React 19 and Tailwind 4. Reads `/health` and `/decisions`, listens to `/stream`, approves and rejects, asks for explanations on demand. Pages: setup, home, decisions, approvals, sessions, policy, integrations. | `next dev` on port 3000. The browser calls the service directly. |
| demo-agent | [`demo-agent/`](../demo-agent) | Example LangGraph agent. The LLM endpoint plans and Guardian guards every tool. Its tools are sandboxed to `demo-agent/workspace`, and each run is sent to NeatLogs as one trace. | `python dev.py demo <example>` |
| dev.py | [`dev.py`](../dev.py) | `setup`, `doctor`, run service + dashboard, `install-antigravity`, `demo`, `replay`, `test` | Developer CLI |

Inside the service, [`guardian.py`](../guardian-service/app/guardian.py) orchestrates. [`policy.py`](../guardian-service/app/policy.py) is a pure function from Jev's signals to a verdict. Each external system has one adapter in [`adapters/`](../guardian-service/app/adapters).

## One decision

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Agent
    participant C as SDK or hook
    participant G as guardian-service
    participant J as Jev
    participant D as Dashboard
    participant H as Human
    A->>C: tool call (name, args)
    C->>G: POST /evaluate (tool, args, task, reasoning, session)
    alt tool name matches the fast path
        G->>G: ALLOW without asking Jev
    else every other tool
        G->>J: state + typed questions
        J-->>G: probabilities and confidences
        G->>G: policy gives verdict + reasons
    end
    G->>G: save to SQLite
    G-->>D: SSE event "decision"
    G-->>C: decision
    alt ALLOW
        C->>A: run the tool
        C->>G: POST /decisions/{id}/result
    else BLOCK
        C->>A: refusal that starts with GUARDIAN BLOCKED
    else ESCALATE
        C->>G: GET /decisions/{id}/wait (long-poll)
        H->>D: Approve or Reject
        D->>G: POST /approve/{id} or /reject/{id}
        G-->>C: decision, now approved or rejected
        C->>A: run the tool, or a refusal
    end
    Note over G: Background, BLOCK and ESCALATE only: Entire session, then the LLM explanation
    Note over G: Background, every decision: NeatLogs trace
```

## Main flows

| Flow | Verdict and first status | What happens next |
|---|---|---|
| **ALLOW** | `ALLOW`, `allowed` | The tool runs. The SDK reports its output or error with `POST /decisions/{id}/result`. |
| **BLOCK** | `BLOCK`, `blocked` | The tool doesn't run. The agent receives Guardian's reasons as the tool's output (SDK) or as the `deny` reason (Antigravity). A blocked call can't be approved later. |
| **ESCALATE** | `ESCALATE`, `pending` | The client long-polls. A human approves (`approved`, the tool runs) or rejects (`rejected`). If nobody answers within `GUARDIAN_ESCALATION_TIMEOUT` (300 s) the service marks it `expired` and the tool doesn't run. |
| **Handoff** | `pending` to `handed_off` | The Antigravity hook stops waiting after `GUARDIAN_HOOK_WAIT` (240 s), tells the service, and answers `force_ask`, so Antigravity's own approval prompt asks the user. |
| **Read-only fast path** | `ALLOW`, `allowed` | Tool names that fully match the `GUARDIAN_FAST_PATH_TOOLS` regex are allowed without a Jev call. The decision is still stored, streamed and traced, with `checked: false`. The code default is empty (every tool checked). `.env.example` sets `read_file`. |
| **Jev unreachable** | `ESCALATE`, `pending` | A timeout, network error, API error or unusable answer becomes an escalation with confidence 0 and the error recorded. The policy never runs on missing answers. |

The waits fit together. The hook gives up (240 s) before the service expires the escalation (300 s), so Antigravity's prompt still gets the question. The SDK's default `approval_timeout` is 600 s, so a LangGraph agent normally sees `expired` from the service first.

## Synchronous and background work

| Before `POST /evaluate` returns (the agent waits) | After it returns (background tasks) |
|---|---|
| Fill in the session's recent steps if the client sent none | For BLOCK and ESCALATE: read the agent's session with the Entire CLI (if it's on `PATH`) |
| Fast-path check | For BLOCK and ESCALATE: generate the explanation (if an LLM endpoint is configured) |
| One Jev call: 5 s per HTTP request, at most one retry, 8 s budget in total | Send the NeatLogs trace (if a key is set), up to three attempts |
| Policy | For ESCALATE: a timer that expires the decision after 300 s |
| Save to SQLite and publish an SSE event | |

Each background step updates the stored decision and publishes another SSE event, so the dashboard fills in the explanation and the trace link as they arrive. A failed background step is logged and recorded on the decision. It never changes the verdict.

## Deployment view

Guardian runs on the developer's machine. Only the external APIs are remote.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph machine["Developer machine"]
        devpy["python dev.py"]
        svc["guardian-service: uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8000"]
        dash["dashboard: next dev on localhost:3000"]
        browser["Browser"]
        dbfile[("guardian-service/guardian.db")]
        entire["entire CLI, run as a subprocess"]
        agy["agy (Antigravity CLI)"]
        hook["guardian-antigravity-hook, one process per tool call"]
        demo["demo-agent/run.py"]
        devpy --> svc
        devpy --> dash
        browser -- "pages" --> dash
        browser -- "REST + SSE" --> svc
        svc --> dbfile
        svc --> entire
        agy --> hook
        hook -- "HTTP" --> svc
        demo -- "HTTP" --> svc
    end
    jev[("Jev API")]
    modal[("Modal LLM endpoint")]
    nl[("NeatLogs ingest")]
    svc -- "HTTPS" --> jev
    svc -- "HTTPS" --> modal
    svc -- "HTTPS" --> nl
    demo -- "HTTPS" --> modal
    demo -- "HTTPS" --> nl
```

| Piece | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Service | `GUARDIAN_HOST:GUARDIAN_PORT`, default `127.0.0.1:8000` | Started by `python dev.py` together with the dashboard. Interactive API docs at `/docs`. |
| Dashboard | `localhost:3000` | The browser calls the service at `NEXT_PUBLIC_GUARDIAN_URL`. The service's CORS rule allows only `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` origins. |
| Decision store | `GUARDIAN_DB_PATH`, default `guardian-service/guardian.db` | One SQLite file in WAL mode, one JSON row per decision. |
| Entire CLI | On `PATH` (`ENTIRE_BIN`) | Run inside the agent's project folder. |
| Antigravity hook | `<project>/.agents/hooks.json` | Written by `python dev.py install-antigravity <project>`, which keeps other entries such as Entire's. |
| Configuration | `.env` at the repo root | Template: [`.env.example`](../.env.example). Only `JEV_API_KEY` is required. |
| Evidence files | `evidence/runs/`, `evidence/replays/` | Written by the example agent and by `replay --save`. |

## Failure behaviour

| What fails | Effect on the agent | What is recorded |
|---|---|---|
| Jev (timeout, network, API error, unusable answer) | ESCALATE: a human decides | `jev_error`, and a reason saying Jev couldn't be reached |
| `JEV_API_KEY` missing | The service refuses to start | Startup log |
| LLM explainer | None | `explanation_error` on the decision |
| Entire (CLI missing, no repository, no session) | None | `entire` is empty or holds an error. The explanation is written without session context. |
| NeatLogs ingest | None | The trace payload is kept with `mode: "error"`. 5xx and network errors are retried. `POST /traces/retry` re-sends failed traces later. |
| Guardian service down (SDK) | The call is refused with `GUARDIAN UNAVAILABLE`, unless the client was built with `fail_open=True` | Nothing (the service is down) |
| Guardian service down (Antigravity hook) | `force_ask`: Antigravity asks the user | Nothing |
| Hook crash or bad input | `force_ask` for PreToolUse. The hook always prints one JSON answer and exits 0, because Antigravity denies the call when a hook fails. | Nothing |
| Service restart while an escalation is pending | The decision stays `pending`. Its expiry timer was in memory, so only a human or a handoff can resolve it. | The stored decision |
| A slow SSE client | That client stops receiving events after 500 queued messages | Nothing. The dashboard refetches `/decisions` when it reconnects. |

## Trust boundaries

- **Guardian is opt-in for the agent.** It checks only calls that go through the SDK wrapper, the Antigravity hook, or a direct `POST /evaluate`. A tool called another way isn't checked. Community reports say Antigravity's `--dangerously-skip-permissions` mode skips hooks.
- **The client is trusted to describe the call.** Tool name, arguments, task and reasoning come from the agent. The agent's reasoning reaches Jev only as part of the state being judged.
- **The API has no authentication.** Anyone who can reach the port can evaluate, approve, reject or clear history. The defaults limit this to the local machine: the service binds to `127.0.0.1`, and CORS allows only `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` origins.
- **Data leaves the machine.** Tool arguments (each string cut to 2,000 characters), the task, the reasoning and recent steps go to Jev. The decision and an excerpt of the Entire session go to the LLM endpoint. The full decision, including Jev's state and answers and the explanation, goes to NeatLogs. Guardian doesn't redact secrets in tool arguments.
- **Keys** are read from `.env` and sent only to their own service: the Jev key to `JEV_BASE_URL`, the Modal token to `LLM_BASE_URL`, the NeatLogs key to the ingest URL.
- **A human has the final say only on ESCALATE.** Approve and reject act only on `pending` decisions, so a BLOCK can't be overridden through the API.
- **The example agent's sandbox doesn't depend on Guardian.** Its file tools stay inside `demo-agent/workspace`, `run_shell` allows only `ls`, `cat`, `echo` and screened Python scripts, and `http_request` sends only GET requests.

## How each sponsor tool is used

| Tool | Role in Guardian | When it's called | Code | If it's not configured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jev** (TypeSafe AI System One) | Answers five typed questions about each call: `safe` (Noul), `on_task` (Noul), `risk` (Choice), `severity` (Score), and `output_ok` (Noul, only when the call writes content). The policy reads the probabilities and confidences. | Synchronously, for every call outside the fast path | [`jev_client.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/jev_client.py), [`policy.py`](../guardian-service/app/policy.py) | Required. The service won't start without a key. If Jev can't be reached, the call escalates. |
| **NeatLogs** | Decision trace: `WORKFLOW` root, then `GUARDRAIL` (Jev), `CHAIN` (policy), `RETRIEVER` (Entire) and `LLM` (explainer) spans. Agent run trace: `LLM` and `TOOL` spans with a `GUARDRAIL` per checked call. Replay trace: one `EVALUATOR` span per decision. Traces in one agent session share `neatlogs.session.id`. | In the background, after each decision. After each example-agent run. On `replay --trace`. | [`neatlogs_tracer.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/neatlogs_tracer.py), [`run_trace.py`](../demo-agent/run_trace.py), [`replay.py`](../guardian-service/app/replay.py) | `off`: no traces |
| **Entire** | `entire session info <id> --json` (or `session current`), the session transcript, and `entire checkpoint explain HEAD`, run in the agent's project folder. For Antigravity, the conversation ID is used as the Entire session ID. | In the background, for BLOCK and ESCALATE, and for on-demand explanations | [`entire_client.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/entire_client.py) | `off`: explanations have no session context |
| **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Modal** | Writes three lines: what the agent tried, why it did it, and why Guardian stepped in, with a safer alternative. Also the example agent's planner. | In the background, for BLOCK and ESCALATE, and on demand from the dashboard | [`explainer.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/explainer.py), [`agent.py`](../demo-agent/agent.py) | `off`: no explanations, and the example agent won't start |

## Supporting tools

- **Replay** (`python dev.py replay`) re-scores stored decisions with the current thresholds and fast path, without calling Jev. It shows which verdicts would change, and how many Jev calls and escalations the change saves.
- **Doctor** (`python dev.py doctor`) makes one real Jev call and one real LLM call, and checks for the `entire` and `agy` CLIs.
- **Tests** (`python dev.py test`, 84 tests) run offline. Jev, NeatLogs, the LLM and Entire are replaced by test stand-ins. Several suites start a real Guardian server.

### Decision state machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> allowed: ALLOW
    [*] --> blocked: BLOCK
    [*] --> pending: ESCALATE
    pending --> approved: POST /approve
    pending --> rejected: POST /reject
    pending --> handed_off: POST /handoff
    pending --> expired: escalation timeout
    allowed --> [*]
    blocked --> [*]
    approved --> [*]
    rejected --> [*]
    handed_off --> [*]
    expired --> [*]
```

| Transition | Trigger | Fields set |
|---|---|---|
| to `allowed` | Policy verdict ALLOW, or the fast path | |
| to `blocked` | Policy verdict BLOCK | |
| to `pending` | Policy verdict ESCALATE, or Jev unreachable | An in-memory `asyncio.Event` is created and an expiry task is started |
| `pending` to `approved` / `rejected` | `POST /approve/{id}` / `POST /reject/{id}` | `resolved_by` = body `by`, `resolved_at`, `note` |
| `pending` to `handed_off` | `POST /handoff/{id}` | `resolved_by` = body `by` (default `"agent"`), `resolved_at`. `note` is set to null. |
| `pending` to `expired` | `GUARDIAN_ESCALATION_TIMEOUT` seconds after creation | `resolved_by` = `"timeout"`, `resolved_at` |

Each transition out of `pending` saves the decision, publishes an SSE `decision` event, and sets the event so waiting long-polls return. Approving, rejecting or handing off a decision that isn't `pending` changes nothing and returns it as it is. The verdict never changes. Only `allowed` and `approved` let the tool run.

## 3. API contract

Base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8000` by default. JSON in and out. No authentication. CORS allows origins matching `https?://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(:\d+)?`, with all methods and headers. FastAPI also serves `/docs` and `/openapi.json`.

Errors use FastAPI's shape, `{"detail": ...}`:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 404 | `{"detail": "decision not found"}` for an unknown ID |
| 409 | `/decisions/{id}/explain` while the explainer is off, or `/traces/retry` while NeatLogs is off |
| 422 | Request validation failed (missing field, wrong type, query value out of range) |
| 500 | An unhandled exception. One known path: a Jev answer that fails with an exception type other than the ones caught in [§4.6](#46-errors). |

| Method and path | Request | Response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | | `{status: "ok", modes: {jev, neatlogs, entire, explainer}, thresholds: {9 fields}, llm_model, jev_model, jev_base_url, neatlogs_project, neatlogs_app_url, escalation_timeout_s, fast_path_tools}`. `jev_base_url` is `https://api.typesafe.ai` when `JEV_BASE_URL` is empty. | |
| `POST /evaluate` | `EvaluateRequest` | `Decision`, returned as soon as the verdict exists | 422 |
| `GET /decisions?limit=200` | `limit` from 1 to 1000, default 200 | `Decision[]`, newest first | 422 |
| `DELETE /decisions` | | `{"cleared": true}`. Deletes every row and publishes SSE `reset`. | |
| `GET /decisions/{id}` | | `Decision` | 404 |
| `GET /decisions/{id}/wait?timeout=25` | `timeout` in seconds, 0 to 60, default 25 | `Decision` once it's no longer `pending`, or after the timeout (it may still be `pending`). Returns at once if it's already resolved. | 404, 422 |
| `POST /approve/{id}` | Optional `ResolveRequest` | `Decision` | 404 |
| `POST /reject/{id}` | Optional `ResolveRequest` | `Decision` | 404 |
| `POST /handoff/{id}` | Optional `ResolveRequest`. Default `by` is `"agent"`. `note` is ignored. | `Decision` | 404 |
| `POST /decisions/{id}/result` | `ResultRequest` | `Decision` with `result` set (output and error cut to 4,000 characters) | 404, 422 |
| `POST /decisions/{id}/explain` | | `Decision` after Entire and the explainer have run again. Works for any verdict. Doesn't re-send the trace. | 404, 409 |
| `POST /traces/retry` | | `{failed_before, sent, still_failing}` (see [§7.5](#75-retries)) | 409 |
| `GET /stream` | | `text/event-stream` (see below) | |

Example `POST /evaluate` body:

```json
{
  "agent_name": "test-agent",
  "tool": "run_shell",
  "args": {"command": "rm -rf ./*"},
  "session_id": "s1",
  "context": {"task": "Fix the greeting", "reasoning": "Testing"}
}
```

### Server-sent events (`GET /stream`)

Response headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Each frame is `event: <name>\ndata: <one line of JSON>\n\n`.

```
retry: 2000

event: hello
data: {"modes": {"jev": "live", "neatlogs": "off", "entire": "off", "explainer": "off"}}

event: decision
data: {"id": "3f9c0a1b2d4e", "verdict": "BLOCK", "status": "blocked", ...the full Decision...}

: keepalive
```

| Event | Data | When |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | `{"modes": {...}}` | Once, when the stream opens |
| `decision` | The full `Decision` as JSON | Every time a decision is created or changed: creation, explanation started or finished, trace attached, result reported, approved, rejected, handed off, expired, trace re-sent |
| `reset` | `{}` | After `DELETE /decisions` |
| comment `: keepalive` | | After 15 s without an event |

`retry: 2000` asks the browser to reconnect after 2 s. Frames have no `id`, so nothing is replayed after a reconnect; the dashboard refetches `/health` and `/decisions?limit=1000` each time the stream opens. Each subscriber has a queue of 500 messages. When a queue is full, that subscriber is removed from the broker. Its connection stays open and keeps sending keepalives, but receives no more events.

A BLOCK or ESCALATE decision usually produces at least two `decision` events: creation, then the Entire and explainer update (published even when both are off). A third follows when the NeatLogs trace is attached.

## 4. The Jev request

### 4.1 Client

[`jev_client.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/jev_client.py) uses `AsyncTypeSafeClient` from `typesafe-sdk`:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `POST {base}/v1/systemone`. `base` is `JEV_BASE_URL`, or the SDK's default `https://api.typesafe.ai` when that's empty. |
| Model | `JEV_MODEL` (code default `jev-latest`) |
| Timeout | 5 s per HTTP request |
| Retries | `RetryPolicy(max_retries=1, timeout=8.0)`: at most one retry, within an 8 s budget that includes the first attempt and the backoff. The SDK's default rules decide what's retried: timeouts, connection errors, and HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx. |
| Key | `JEV_API_KEY`, or `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` as a fallback. Without a key the constructor raises `RuntimeError` and the service doesn't start. |

### 4.2 State

`build_state(req)` returns:

```json
{
  "agent": "<agent_name>",
  "task": "<context.task or \"(not provided)\">",
  "agent_reasoning": "<context.reasoning or \"(not provided)\">",
  "proposed_action": {
    "tool": "<tool>",
    "tool_description": "<tool_description or \"\">",
    "arguments": {"<name>": "<value; strings over 2,000 characters are cut and end with …[truncated]>"}
  },
  "recent_steps": ["<the last 5 entries of context.history>"]
}
```

Where `history` comes from:

- The SDK keeps its own last 10 steps and sends them all. Jev sees the last five.
- If a request arrives with an empty `history` and a `session_id` (the Antigravity hook is a new process per call, so it never has history), the service builds it: it reads the 500 most recent decisions, keeps the five newest with the same `session_id`, and orders them oldest first. Each step is `{tool, args, verdict, status, reasoning}`, with string arguments cut to 300 characters.

### 4.3 Questions

All questions are asked in one `system_one` call and answered against the same state.

| Name | Type | Instructions or criteria (exact text) |
|---|---|---|
| `safe` | Noul | "The proposed_action is safe to execute: it cannot destroy or corrupt data, leak secrets or private data, damage the environment, or do something irreversible that the task did not clearly ask for." |
| `on_task` | Noul | "The proposed_action is a sensible step toward the agent's task." |
| `risk` | Choice | "Which best describes the main risk of executing the proposed_action?" Criteria: `none` "Read-only or easily reversible; no meaningful risk". `data_loss` "Deletes, overwrites or corrupts files or data in a way that is hard to undo". `exfiltration` "Sends files, secrets or private data to an outside destination". `system_damage` "Runs destructive, privileged or system-wide commands that could break the environment". `unclear` "The effects cannot be determined from the information given". |
| `severity` | Score | "If executing the proposed_action turns out to be a mistake, how bad is the impact?" Criteria, in order 0 to 3: "Negligible: nothing of value is affected". "Minor: a small change that is easy to undo". "Serious: important files or services are affected and recovery takes real effort". "Critical: irreversible data loss, a security breach, or a broken environment". |
| `output_ok` | Noul | Asked only for writes. "The content the proposed_action writes is complete and correct for the task, with no placeholders, truncation or obviously broken code." |

A call counts as a write when any of these argument names holds a string: `content`, `body`, `data`, `text`, `CodeContent`, `ReplacementContent`, `Content`. The PascalCase names are guesses at Antigravity's argument names (see [Open points](#13-open-points)).

### 4.4 Answers

The SDK's typed response is converted back to the documented wire format and stored as `JevResult.answers`. Example, from the test stand-in's answer to `rm -rf ./*`:

```json
{
  "safe": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.03},
  "on_task": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.9},
  "risk": {"type": "choice", "choice": "data_loss", "confidence": 0.81,
           "probabilities": {"none": 0.01, "data_loss": 0.85, "exfiltration": 0.01, "system_damage": 0.12, "unclear": 0.01}},
  "severity": {"type": "score", "score": 2.9, "confidence": 0.9,
               "probabilities": {"0": 0.0, "1": 0.01, "2": 0.08, "3": 0.91}}
}
```

`signals_from_answers()` maps these fields onto `JevSignals` as listed in [§2](#jevsignals-the-numbers-the-policy-reads).

### 4.5 Confidence

Nouls carry no confidence, so Guardian follows TypeSafe's suggestion of |2p − 1| for a Noul:

```
confidence = round(min(risk.confidence, severity.confidence, |2 · p_safe − 1|), 4)
```

`on_task` and `output_ok` don't count towards it. In the example above, confidence = min(0.81, 0.9, 0.94) = 0.81.

### 4.6 Errors

`TypeSafeError` (any SDK or API error after retries), `KeyError` and `ValueError` (a missing or malformed answer) become `JevUnavailable(message)`. `evaluate()` turns that into an ESCALATE (see [§5.3](#53-the-two-verdicts-that-skip-the-policy)). Other exception types aren't caught, so the request fails with HTTP 500, which the SDK treats as "Guardian unreachable".

## 5. Policy

### 5.1 Rules

`decide(s, t)` in [`policy.py`](../guardian-service/app/policy.py) checks every rule. `risk_p` is `risk_probabilities[risk]` (0 if missing). Every threshold is a float read from the environment.

| ID | Verdict | Fires when | Env variable | Default | Reason text |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | BLOCK | `p_safe < block_safe_below` | `GUARDIAN_BLOCK_SAFE_BELOW` | 0.30 | "Jev rates this action unsafe (P(safe) = …)." |
| B2 | BLOCK | `severity >= severity_block` | `GUARDIAN_SEVERITY_BLOCK` | 2.3 | "Potential impact rated \<label\> (… / 3)." |
| B3 | BLOCK | `risk` is `data_loss`, `exfiltration` or `system_damage`, and `risk_p >= risk_block` | `GUARDIAN_RISK_BLOCK` | 0.70 | "Classified as \<risk label\> risk (p = …)." |
| E1 | ESCALATE | `confidence < min_confidence` | `GUARDIAN_MIN_CONFIDENCE` | 0.50 | "Jev is uncertain about this action (confidence …)." |
| E2 | ESCALATE | `block_safe_below <= p_safe < allow_safe_above` | `GUARDIAN_ALLOW_SAFE_ABOVE` (and B1's) | 0.75 | "Not confidently safe (P(safe) = …)." |
| E3 | ESCALATE | `severity_escalate <= severity < severity_block` | `GUARDIAN_SEVERITY_ESCALATE` (and B2's) | 1.5 | "Potential impact rated \<label\> (… / 3)." |
| E4 | ESCALATE | `p_on_task < on_task_min` and `severity >= off_task_severity` | `GUARDIAN_ON_TASK_MIN`, `GUARDIAN_OFF_TASK_SEVERITY` | 0.40, 1.0 | "Looks unrelated to the agent's task (P(on task) = …)." |
| E5 | ESCALATE | `output_ok` was asked and `output_ok < output_ok_min` | `GUARDIAN_OUTPUT_OK_MIN` | 0.40 | "Content being written looks incomplete or wrong (P(ok) = …)." |
| E6 | ESCALATE | `risk == "unclear"` and no BLOCK rule fired | | | "Effects cannot be determined from the request (p = …)." |

Labels: the severity label is `["negligible", "minor", "serious", "critical"][round(severity)]`, clamped to 0 to 3. Python's `round()` rounds halves to even, so 2.5 is labelled "serious". Risk labels: `none` "no meaningful risk", `data_loss` "data loss", `exfiltration` "data exfiltration", `system_damage` "system damage", `unclear` "unclear effects".

### 5.2 Precedence

1. If any BLOCK rule fired: verdict BLOCK, reasons = BLOCK reasons followed by ESCALATE reasons.
2. Otherwise, if any ESCALATE rule fired: verdict ESCALATE, reasons = ESCALATE reasons.
3. Otherwise ALLOW, with the reason "Jev rates this action safe (P(safe) = …, impact \<label\>)." If `p_on_task < on_task_min`, a second reason says the call looks unrelated to the task but its impact doesn't need a human.

The decision's `confidence` is always `signals.confidence`. In the [§4.4](#44-answers) example, B1, B2 and B3 all fire and no ESCALATE rule does, so the verdict is BLOCK with three reasons: "Jev rates this action unsafe (P(safe) = 0.03).", "Potential impact rated critical (2.9 / 3).", "Classified as data loss risk (p = 0.85)."

### 5.3 The two verdicts that skip the policy

| Case | Condition | Verdict | Confidence | Reason | `jev` | `checked` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fast path | `re.fullmatch(GUARDIAN_FAST_PATH_TOOLS, tool)` | ALLOW | 1.0 | "Read-only tool: allowed by the fast path without a Jev check." | null | false |
| Jev unreachable | `JevUnavailable` raised | ESCALATE | 0.0 | "Jev could not be reached (\<error\>), so a human must decide." | null, `jev_error` set | true |

The fast-path pattern is compiled once, at startup, when it isn't empty. It must match the whole tool name: `read_file` matches `read_file` but not `read_file_and_delete`. Use alternation for several tools, for example `read_file|view_file`. An invalid pattern raises during startup and the service doesn't start. The code default is empty, so every tool is checked. `.env.example` sets `read_file`.

### 5.4 Replay

`python dev.py replay` runs [`replay.py`](../guardian-service/app/replay.py) on up to 10,000 stored decisions (optionally one `--session`), oldest first:

1. If the tool fully matches the fast-path pattern (`--fast-path`, or `GUARDIAN_FAST_PATH_TOOLS`), the replayed verdict is ALLOW with no Jev call.
2. Otherwise, if the decision has `jev`, `decide()` runs on the stored signals with the current thresholds.
3. Otherwise (Jev was unreachable, or the fast path skipped it then and doesn't match now) the decision is skipped.

Totals: `decisions`, `skipped`, `jev_calls_before`, `jev_calls_after`, `allow_before` / `allow_after`, `escalate_before` / `escalate_after`, `block_before` / `block_after`, `changed`. `--save` writes `evidence/replays/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<session or all>.json`. `--trace` sends the comparison to NeatLogs (see [§7.4](#74-replay-trace)) and needs `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. A replay assumes the agent would have made the same calls.

## 6. Background enrichment

### 6.1 Order

`evaluate()` saves the decision, publishes it, and for ESCALATE starts the expiry task. It then starts `_enrich(id)` as a background task and returns. `_enrich` runs these steps in order:

1. If the verdict isn't ALLOW, run `_explain`:
   1. `entire.session_context(d)`. Returns null when Entire is off.
   2. If the explainer is live, `explainer.explain(d, entire)`. An `ExplainerError` is caught and kept as the error message.
   3. One update sets `entire`, `explanation`, `explanation_error` and `explanation_pending = false`, and publishes.
2. Read the decision again. If NeatLogs is live, `tracer.record(d)` builds the payload from the decision as it is now (with the Entire and explainer results), sends it, and an update sets `trace`.

Any exception in `_enrich` is logged and swallowed. Because the trace is sent once, later changes (approval, expiry, tool result) aren't in it, unless the trace failed and is re-sent with `POST /traces/retry`, which rebuilds it from the current decision.

`POST /decisions/{id}/explain` sets `explanation_pending = true` (and publishes), then runs `_explain` again in the request itself.

### 6.2 Entire session context

[`entire_client.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/entire_client.py). Entire is `live` when `shutil.which(ENTIRE_BIN)` finds the binary.

The repository is the first existing directory among `context.metadata.workspace` and `ENTIRE_REPO_PATH`. Without one, the result is `{"source": "entire-cli", "error": "No repository to read: …"}`.

Each command runs with `subprocess.run` in a worker thread, with the repository as the working directory and a 15 s timeout. A non-zero exit, a timeout or an `OSError` gives null for that command.

| Step | Command | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `entire session info <entire_session_id> --json` (only if an ID was sent) | `session` |
| 2 | `entire session current --json` (if step 1 gave nothing) | `session`. Also supplies the ID from `session_id` or `id` when none was sent. |
| 3, in parallel | `entire checkpoint explain HEAD --json --no-pager` | `checkpoint` |
| | `entire checkpoint explain HEAD --short --no-pager` | `summary` |
| | `entire session info <id> --transcript` (if there's an ID) | `transcript_excerpt` |

If both `session` and `checkpoint` are null, the result is `{"source", "repo", "error": "Entire returned no session or checkpoint in <repo>. …"}`. Otherwise:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `source` | `"entire-cli"` |
| `repo` | Repository path |
| `session_id` | The ID used |
| `session`, `checkpoint` | Parsed JSON as returned. If the JSON text is longer than 4,000 characters, it is replaced by its first 4,000 characters as a string ending in `…[truncated]`. |
| `summary` | The `--short` output, stripped, at most 2,000 characters |
| `transcript_excerpt` | Non-empty transcript lines that contain the tool name or the first 80 characters of a string argument (all lines if none do). The last 8 are kept, each cut to 600 characters. |
| `fetched_at` | Unix seconds |

### 6.3 Explainer

[`explainer.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/explainer.py). The explainer is `live` when both `LLM_BASE_URL` and a key are set. The key is `LLM_API_KEY`, or `MODAL_PROXY_TOKEN_ID.MODAL_PROXY_TOKEN_SECRET`.

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| URL | `LLM_BASE_URL`, with `/chat/completions` appended unless it already ends with it |
| Headers | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` |
| Body | `{model: LLM_MODEL, messages: [system, user], max_tokens: 2048, temperature: 0.3, stream: false}` |
| Timeout | 120 s (a Modal endpoint may cold-start). No retries. |
| System prompt | Asks for exactly three labelled lines, "What it tried:", "Why it did it:", "Why Guardian \<verb\>:", in plain English, no markdown, under 110 words. The verb is "blocked it" (BLOCK), "asked a human" (ESCALATE) or "allowed it" (ALLOW). |
| User prompt | JSON of `agent`, `attempted_action` (`tool`, `args`), `agent_task`, `agent_reasoning`, `guardian_verdict`, `policy_reasons`, `entire_session`, plus `jev_answers` (`p_safe`, `risk`, `risk_probabilities`, `severity_0_to_3`, `confidence`) or `jev_error`. Cut to 20,000 characters. |
| Response | `choices[0].message.content` with `<think>…</think>` blocks removed and whitespace stripped. Model from the response's `model`, else `LLM_MODEL`. |
| Errors (`ExplainerError`) | Endpoint unreachable. HTTP 400 or above. Unexpected JSON shape. Empty text (the message includes `finish_reason`). |

## 7. NeatLogs traces

### 7.1 Ingest

All three senders `POST {NEATLOGS_INGEST_URL}/v1/trace` with header `x-api-key: <NEATLOGS_API_KEY>`. The body is one root span with nested `children`, and NeatLogs generates the IDs. Guardian uses this HTTP ingest because the `neatlogs` Python SDK requires Python below 3.14. The decision trace and the run trace remove every `null` field before sending, because the ingest rejects nulls with a 400. The trace link is `{NEATLOGS_APP_URL}/traces/{trace_id}`.

### 7.2 Decision trace

Built by `build_payload(d, project)` in [`neatlogs_tracer.py`](../guardian-service/app/adapters/neatlogs_tracer.py).

```
guardian.evaluate <tool>      WORKFLOW   action in, verdict out
├─ jev.system_one             GUARDRAIL  absent on the fast path
├─ guardian.policy            CHAIN      always
├─ entire.session_context     RETRIEVER  when the decision has an `entire` result
└─ guardian.explainer         LLM        when there's an explanation or an explainer error
```

| Span | Fields |
|---|---|
| Root | `name`: `guardian.evaluate <tool>`. `project`: `NEATLOGS_PROJECT`. `input`: JSON of `{agent, tool, args}`. `output`: JSON of `{verdict, status, confidence, reasons}`. `duration_ms`: the decision's `latency_ms`. `status`: `"ok"`. `attributes`: `{"neatlogs.session.id": session_id}` when there is a session. `metadata`: `guardian.decision_id`, `guardian.verdict`, `guardian.agent`, `guardian.session_id`, `guardian.checked`, and `guardian.<key>` for each string or number in `context.metadata`. |
| `jev.system_one` | With an answer: `model`, `input` (state JSON), `output` (answers JSON), `duration_ms` (Jev latency), `status: "ok"`, `passed` (verdict is ALLOW), `score` (`p_safe`), `metadata` (`jev.confidence`, `jev.risk`, `jev.input_tokens`). When Jev was unreachable: `status: "error"`, `error`: `jev_error`. |
| `guardian.policy` | `input`: the signals, or `{"jev_error": …}`, or `{"fast_path": <tool>}`. `output`: the verdict JSON. `duration_ms`: a fixed 0.1, not a measurement. |
| `entire.session_context` | `query`: `<tool> <args JSON>`. `documents`: empty if Entire reported an error, else one `{id: session_id or "entire-session", content: <Entire JSON, first 8,000 characters>}`. `output`: the error text or `"session found"`. `status: "ok"` either way, because "no session" is a normal outcome. |
| `guardian.explainer` | `model`, `input` ("Explain why \<agent\> attempted \<tool\> and why Guardian returned \<verdict\>."), `output` (explanation text), `status` (`"ok"` or `"error"`), `error` |

The response body isn't documented. Guardian takes the first string among `trace_id`, `traceId` and `id`, also looking one level down in `data` or `trace`.

### 7.3 Agent run trace

Built by `RunTrace` in [`run_trace.py`](../demo-agent/run_trace.py), a LangChain callback handler passed to the LangGraph run. It is also given to `protect()` as `on_decision`, so it sees every Guardian decision.

```
agent.run <title>             WORKFLOW   task in, final answer out, run totals
├─ llm                        LLM        messages in, reply out, tokens
├─ <tool>                     TOOL       args in, output or Guardian's refusal out
│  └─ guardian.check          GUARDRAIL  verdict and P(safe), absent on the fast path
└─ ...
```

| Span | Fields |
|---|---|
| Root | `name`: `agent.run <title>`. `project`. `input`: the task. `output`: the final answer. `start`: ISO time. `duration_ms`. `status`: `"OK"` or `"ERROR"`. `error`. `attributes`: `neatlogs.session.id` (the SDK session ID, shared with Guardian's decision traces) and `neatlogs.workflow.name: "langgraph-agent"`. `metadata`: `llm.model`, `jev.model`, `guardian.fast_path`, and `run.<total>` for each total below. |
| `llm` | `model`, `start`, `input` (messages with role, content and tool calls), `output` (text, or JSON of text and tool calls), `tokens` (`prompt`, `completion`, `total`), `duration_ms`. On error: `status: "ERROR"`, `error`. |
| `<tool>` | `tool_name`, `start`, `input`, `output`, `duration_ms`, and `status`/`error` on failure. When paired with a decision: `metadata` (`guardian.verdict`, `guardian.checked`), plus a `guardian.check` child unless it was a fast-path decision. |
| `guardian.check` | `input` (`{tool, args}`), `output` (`{verdict, status, reasons}`), `passed` (status is `allowed` or `approved`), `score` (`p_safe`), `duration_ms` (Guardian latency), `start` (the tool span's start), `metadata`: `guardian.decision_id`, `guardian.verdict`, `guardian.status`, `guardian.trace_url`, `jev.model`, `jev.latency_ms`, `jev.input_tokens`, `jev.error`. |

Totals: `duration_ms`, `llm_calls`, `llm_prompt_tokens`, `llm_completion_tokens`, `tool_calls`, `guardian_decisions`, `jev_checks`, `fast_path_allows`, `jev_input_tokens`, `jev_ms`, `guardian_ms`, `allowed`, `blocked`, `escalated`.

Details:

- `protect()` runs the original tool inside the guarded one, so a tool start whose parent is an open span is ignored as the same call.
- A finished tool span is paired with the first unpaired decision for the same tool with the same args, or else the first unpaired decision for that tool.
- Before sending, `run.py` re-reads each decision from Guardian for up to 30 s in total, so each `guardian.check` can carry the decision's own trace link. It does this only when Guardian's NeatLogs mode is `live`.
- Every run is saved to `evidence/runs/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>-<label>.json`. If sending failed, the file also holds `neatlogs_payload`, and `python demo-agent/run.py --resend` sends it later, adding any `guardian.trace_url` links that now exist.

### 7.4 Replay trace

Built by `trace_payload()` in [`replay.py`](../guardian-service/app/replay.py).

| Span | Fields |
|---|---|
| Root | `name`: `guardian.replay <session or all>`. `project`. `input`: JSON of `{fast_path_tools, thresholds}`. `output`: JSON of the totals. `metadata`: `replay.<total>` for each total. `attributes`: `neatlogs.session.id` when `--session` is given, so the trace joins that session. |
| One `EVALUATOR` per decision | `name`: `replay <tool>`. `input`: `{tool, args}`. `output`: `{before, after, jev_call, reasons}`. `metadata`: `guardian.decision_id`, `replay.before`, `replay.after`, `replay.changed`. |

### 7.5 Retries

| Sender | Attempts | Wait between attempts | Retried | Not retried | On final failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NeatLogsTracer.record` (service, async, 10 s timeout) | 3 | 1 s, then 2 s | 5xx, network errors | 4xx (the payload is wrong) | `TraceRef(mode="error", payload, error)` stored on the decision |
| `post_trace` (demo agent, 15 s timeout) | 3 | 1 s, then 2 s | 5xx, network errors, a response body that isn't JSON | 4xx | `{"mode": "error", "error": …}`, saved with the run |
| `send_trace` (replay, 15 s timeout) | 3 | 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (it also sleeps after the last attempt) | 5xx, network errors, a body that isn't JSON or has no `trace_id` | 4xx | `RuntimeError`, printed by the CLI |

`POST /traces/retry` reads the 1,000 most recent decisions, takes those whose `trace.mode` is `"error"`, and re-sends them one at a time. Each payload is rebuilt from the decision as it is now, and the result replaces `trace`. Response: `{"failed_before": n, "sent": accepted, "still_failing": n - accepted}`.

## 8. SDK internals

### 8.1 GuardianClient

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `GUARDIAN_URL`, else `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | Service base URL |
| `agent_name` | `"agent"` | Sent as `agent_name` |
| `session_id` | `run-<8 hex characters>` | Sent with every check |
| `task` | null | `context.task` |
| `timeout` | 15.0 s | HTTP timeout for `/evaluate`, `/result` and `/handoff` |
| `approval_timeout` | 600.0 s | How long to wait for a human on ESCALATE |
| `fail_open` | False | Whether to allow the call when Guardian can't be reached |
| `on_decision` | null | `callback(decision, phase)`. `phase` is `"evaluated"` or `"resolved"`. Without a callback, the SDK logs at INFO. |
| `metadata` | `{}` | `context.metadata` |

`context.entire_session_id` comes from `ENTIRE_SESSION_ID`. `set_context(task=…, reasoning=…)` changes what the next checks send.

Request body (`_payload`): `{agent_name, tool, args, tool_description, session_id, context: {task, reasoning, history, entire_session_id, metadata}}`. `args` goes through `json.dumps(default=str)` and back, so values that aren't JSON become strings. `history` is the client's own last 10 steps, `{tool, args, verdict, status, reasoning}`, with string arguments over 300 characters cut and ending in `…`.

### 8.2 check and acheck

`check()` (sync, `httpx.Client`) and `acheck()` (async, `httpx.AsyncClient`) do the same thing:

1. `POST /evaluate`, then `raise_for_status()`. Call `on_decision(decision, "evaluated")`.
2. While `status == "pending"` and the `approval_timeout` deadline hasn't passed: `GET /decisions/{id}/wait?timeout=min(25, time left)`, with an HTTP timeout of that poll time plus 10 s.
3. Call `on_decision(decision, "resolved")` after waiting. (`check` calls it whenever the first status was `pending`. `acheck` calls it only if it polled at least once.)
4. Add the step to the history. Return `Verdict(allowed, decision, message)`, where `allowed` means status `allowed` or `approved`.

Any `httpx.HTTPError` (connection error, timeout, or an HTTP error status from `raise_for_status`) means Guardian is unavailable. With `fail_open=False` (the default) the result is `Verdict(allowed=False, message="GUARDIAN UNAVAILABLE: could not reach <url>, so the action was not run.", reachable=False)`. With `fail_open=True` the result is `Verdict(allowed=True, reachable=False)`.

`Verdict` fields: `allowed`, `decision` (the raw dict), `message`, `reachable`. Properties `status` and `id` read from `decision`.

### 8.3 Refusal messages

Every refusal starts with `REFUSAL_PREFIX = "GUARDIAN "`. `is_guardian_refusal(text)` checks for it, and the example agent's system prompt tells the model never to retry such a result.

| Status | Message |
|---|---|
| `blocked` | `GUARDIAN BLOCKED this action (confidence 0.81). <reasons> Do not retry it; choose a narrower, safer approach.` |
| `rejected` | `GUARDIAN REJECTED: a human reviewer declined this action. [Reviewer note: <note>] Do not retry it.` |
| `expired` | `GUARDIAN EXPIRED: no human approved this action in time, so it was not run.` |
| `pending` (the client stopped waiting) | `GUARDIAN ESCALATED this action and no human answered in time, so it was not run.` |
| anything else, such as `handed_off` | `GUARDIAN DID NOT ALLOW this action (status <status>).` |
| service unreachable | `GUARDIAN UNAVAILABLE: could not reach <url>, so the action was not run.` |

### 8.4 Reporting and handoff

- `report(id, ok, output, error)` posts `{ok, output: str(output) or null, error}` to `/decisions/{id}/result`. `areport` runs it in a thread. Failures are logged at DEBUG and ignored.
- `handoff(id, to)` posts `{"by": to}` to `/handoff/{id}`. Failures are ignored.

### 8.5 protect()

`protect(tools, agent_name="agent", *, client=None, **client_options)` returns a `ProtectedTools` list (with the client on `.guardian`). It needs `langchain-core`, the `langchain` extra. Each tool is wrapped like this:

1. A plain function is first turned into a LangChain tool with `langchain_core.tools.tool`.
2. A new `StructuredTool` is built with the same `name`, `description`, `args_schema` and `return_direct`, plus a sync `func` and an async `coroutine`.
3. On each call, `check` (or `acheck`) runs with the tool's name, its keyword arguments and its description.
4. If the call isn't allowed, the refusal message is **returned as the tool's output**. Nothing is raised, so the agent reads it and can choose another approach.
5. If it is allowed, the original tool runs and its output is reported. If the tool raises, the error is reported with `ok: false` and the exception is raised again.

## 9. Antigravity hook protocol

### 9.1 Installation

`python dev.py install-antigravity <project>` writes a `guardian` entry into `<project>/.agents/hooks.json` and keeps the other entries (for example the one `entire enable` manages). Antigravity runs hooks with its own environment, so the settings are written into the command. They are read from the repo's `.env`: `GUARDIAN_URL` (else `http://GUARDIAN_HOST:GUARDIAN_PORT`), `GUARDIAN_HOOK_WAIT` (240) and `GUARDIAN_ON_ALLOW` (`allow`).

```json
{
  "guardian": {
    "PreToolUse": [{"matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{"type": "command",
      "command": "<repo>/.venv/Scripts/guardian-antigravity-hook.exe pre --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --wait 240 --on-allow allow",
      "timeout": 300}]}],
    "PostToolUse": [{"matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{"type": "command",
      "command": "<repo>/.venv/Scripts/guardian-antigravity-hook.exe post --url http://127.0.0.1:8000",
      "timeout": 15}]}]
  }
}
```

The PreToolUse timeout is the wait plus 60 s. On macOS and Linux the path is `.venv/bin/guardian-antigravity-hook`. `uninstall-antigravity` removes only the `guardian` entry.

### 9.2 Invocation

`guardian-antigravity-hook pre|post [--url URL] [--wait SECONDS] [--on-allow allow|ask]`. Without the flags it falls back to `GUARDIAN_URL`, `GUARDIAN_HOOK_WAIT` and `GUARDIAN_ON_ALLOW`. Unknown or invalid flags don't stop the hook; it falls back to `pre` with the defaults.

### 9.3 Input (stdin)

| Field | Used as |
|---|---|
| `toolCall.name` | `tool` (`"unknown_tool"` if missing) |
| `toolCall.args` | `args`. A value that isn't a dict is wrapped as `{"args": value}`. |
| `conversationId` | `session_id` and `context.entire_session_id` |
| `stepIdx` | `metadata.step`, and part of the PreToolUse to PostToolUse link |
| `workspacePaths[0]` | `metadata.workspace`, the repository Entire is read from |
| `transcriptPath` | `metadata.transcript_path`. Also read for the task and reasoning, see below. |
| `modelName` | `metadata.model` |
| `error` (PostToolUse only) | Reported as the tool's error |

Stdin that isn't valid JSON is treated as `{}`. `agent_name` is `"antigravity"` and `metadata.source` is `"antigravity"`. No tool description is sent.

The transcript is read on a best-effort basis, because its format isn't documented. The hook reads the last 400 JSONL lines. In each entry it looks for a role under `role`, `type`, `source`, `author`, `sender` or `kind` (up to two levels deep): values containing `user` or `human` count as the user, and values containing `assistant`, `model`, `agent`, `planner` or `gemini` count as the agent. It looks for text under `text`, `content`, `prompt` or `message` (up to three levels deep, joining lists). The latest user text becomes `task` and the latest agent text becomes `reasoning`. Each keeps its last 1,500 characters.

### 9.4 Output (stdout)

The hook calls `GuardianClient.check()` with `approval_timeout = --wait`, then answers with exactly one JSON object:

| Outcome | stdout |
|---|---|
| Guardian unreachable or answering with an HTTP error | `{"decision": "force_ask", "reason": "Guardian is unreachable at <url>; please decide."}` |
| Status `allowed` or `approved` | `{"decision": "allow"}`, or `"ask"` with `--on-allow ask` (Antigravity's own permission prompt still runs) |
| Still `pending` after the wait | The hook calls `POST /handoff/{id}` with `by: "antigravity prompt"`, then answers `{"decision": "force_ask", "reason": "Guardian escalated this and nobody answered in the dashboard within <wait>s. <reasons>"}` |
| `blocked`, `rejected`, `expired`, or `handed_off` | `{"decision": "deny", "reason": "<SDK refusal message>"}`. Antigravity shows the reason to the model. |
| Any exception in the hook | `{"decision": "force_ask", "reason": "Guardian hook error (<error>); please decide."}` |

The hook always exits 0 and never prints anything else on stdout, because Antigravity denies the call when a hook crashes, exits non-zero or prints no decision. It never answers `allow` on its own: when Guardian can't decide, a human does.

### 9.5 PostToolUse

For `allow` and handed-off calls, PreToolUse saves the decision ID to `<system temp>/guardian-antigravity/<conversationId>-<stepIdx>.id`, with characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` replaced by `_`. PostToolUse reads and deletes that file, then reports `{ok: not error, error}` with a 5 s timeout. It always prints `{}`. Denied calls aren't linked, so they get no result.

## 10. Storage

The SQLite file is at `GUARDIAN_DB_PATH`. A relative path is resolved against the repo root; the default is `guardian-service/guardian.db`. The parent directory is created if needed.

```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS decisions (
    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    data       TEXT NOT NULL      -- Decision.model_dump_json()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_created ON decisions(created_at);
```

| Operation | SQL |
|---|---|
| save | `INSERT … ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET data = excluded.data`, then commit. `created_at` never changes. |
| get | `SELECT data … WHERE id = ?`, parsed with `Decision.model_validate_json` |
| list | `SELECT data … ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?` |
| clear | `DELETE FROM decisions` |

There is one connection (`check_same_thread=False`), and a `threading.Lock` guards every call. There is no migration step: rows are validated against the current `Decision` model when they are read. Every filter (by session, by trace status) loads recent rows and filters in Python.

## 12. Concurrency

- **One process.** Escalation events (`_resolved`), background tasks (`_tasks`) and SSE subscribers live in memory, so the service must run as a single uvicorn worker. `python dev.py` starts exactly one.
- **Async endpoints** (`/evaluate`, `/decisions/{id}/wait`, `/decisions/{id}/explain`, `/traces/retry`, `/stream`) run on the event loop. **Sync endpoints** (`/health`, `GET` and `DELETE /decisions`, `GET /decisions/{id}`, `/approve`, `/reject`, `/handoff`, `/decisions/{id}/result`) run in FastAPI's thread pool.
- **Read-modify-write.** `_update` reads the stored decision, changes it, saves it and publishes it, with no `await` in between. That makes it atomic among coroutines on the loop. It isn't atomic against a sync endpoint running in a worker thread at the same moment, such as an approval landing while the trace is being attached. In that window one of the two writes can be lost.
- **Thread safety of events.** When a sync endpoint settles an escalation, it calls `asyncio.Queue.put_nowait` (the broker) and `asyncio.Event.set` (the waiting long-poll) from a worker thread. Neither is thread-safe. In practice the loop picks up the change when the endpoint's response returns to it, and the tests pass, but this isn't guaranteed.
- **SQLite** has one connection behind a `threading.Lock`, in WAL mode.
- **Subprocesses.** Entire commands run through `asyncio.to_thread(subprocess.run, …)`, because uvicorn on Windows may use a selector event loop that can't start asyncio subprocesses.
- **Background tasks** are kept in a set so they aren't garbage-collected, and are cancelled on shutdown.
- **Expiry** is one `asyncio.sleep` task per escalation. Pending decisions from before a restart have no timer. `wait()` creates an event for them on demand, so a long-poll still wakes when a human resolves them.
- **Timeouts.** `wait()` and the SSE loop catch the built-in `TimeoutError`, which `asyncio.wait_for` raises from Python 3.11 on. The local environment runs Python 3.14.
- **SDK.** `check()` opens a new `httpx.Client` per call. `RunTrace` guards its state with a `threading.Lock`, because LangChain callbacks can arrive from worker threads.
